case.title: A hidden source in NGC 4945 that has flared in the infrared every 5.4 years: three outbursts with a sudden rise
case.hook: Found blind by Oddsky's search for repeating infrared sources in nearby galaxies (hunt H-0013): WISE sees cycles peaking in 2011, 2016-17 and 2022, and Spitzer caught the 2016 rise, a jump of 25x in under half a year. Nothing is catalogued at the position. Next peak expected around 2027.5.
case.summary: An infrared source in the dusty edge-on starburst galaxy NGC 4945 (3.8 Mpc) that brightens sharply every 5.4 years: WISE saw cycles in 2011, 2016-17 and 2022, and Spitzer caught the 2016 rise. Each swing is about 3e5 L_sun, with no optical counterpart. Most likely a massive binary forming dust at each close approach; an extreme dusty pulsating star is the alternative. Next peak expected around 2027.5. Found blind by Oddsky hunt H-0013.

claims.text: WISE (unWISE neo11 difference photometry, H-0012/H-0013): three cycles peaking 2011.27, 2016.71 and 2022.14, a period of 5.43 yr (WISE) and 5.37 yr (joint WISE + Spitzer fit), with a sawtooth shape: fast rise (about 8% of the period), slower decline, short minimum (hunts/H-0013/README.md).
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Spitzer/IRAC warm mission 2012-2019 tracks two cycles: from +22 to +505 (3.6 um) / +748 uJy (4.5 um) between 2016.34 and 2016.78, a rise in under 0.45 yr; a single 2007.6 [4.5] epoch fits the decline of a 2005.9 cycle.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Peak-to-trough W2 amplitude about 3e5 L_sun at 3.8 Mpc. The light-curve shape test favours a flat-minimum outburst train over a sinusoid (Z_joint = +83). Luminous dusty long-period variables reach P = 1,000-2,500 d and nu L_nu(4.5 um) of order 1e5-5e5 L_sun (Karambelkar et al. 2019, SPIRITS), so pulsation is not excluded by luminosity alone.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: No optical or near-infrared counterpart: nothing in Gaia DR3 or HST at the position, in the dust lane of an edge-on starburst; a Galactic foreground star (b = +13 deg) is implausible with no Gaia source and P = 5.4 yr.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Not reported (2026-11-02): ADS full text for the coordinates and for the host with variability terms finds nothing on this source; nothing in TNS, SIMBAD, Gaia DR3, AllWISE or the Spitzer SEIP catalogue at the position; the SPIRITS catalogue of luminous long-period variables (Karambelkar et al. 2019) does not cover this galaxy.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A massive colliding-wind binary forming dust at each periastron every 5.4 yr, deeply embedded in NGC 4945.
hypotheses.would_falsify: An infrared spectrum with silicate or SiC features (AGB dust), or no brightening in 2026.8-2028.3.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: An extremely luminous dusty long-period variable (super-AGB star or red supergiant with extreme mass loss).
hypotheses.would_falsify: Already strained by the fast rise and flat minimum, which pulsators do not show.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.would_falsify: Two observatories see the same cycles at one position.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

figures.caption: WISE (blue) and Spitzer/IRAC (red) brightness changes at 3.4/3.6 µm (top) and 4.6/4.5 µm (bottom). The curves are the fitted recurring outburst, with a period of 5.4 years; vertical lines mark the fitted outburst times. Centre: the Spitzer median image and the bright-minus-faint difference, in which the variable is a point source. Right: how much the fit improves against trial period. This is the hunt's working diagnostic plot, shown as produced.
figures.alt: WISE and Spitzer light curves with a repeating sawtooth model, image cutouts and a period scan.
